rich_summary: As King Sagara’s sixty thousand sons dig through the earth searching for the stolen sacrificial horse, their violence throws the cosmos into turmoil. Devas, gandharvas, nagas, and other beings appeal to Brahma, who explains that the princes are doomed: the world is upheld by Vasudeva in the form of the sage Kapila, and the reckless princes will meet his wrath. Ignoring restraint, they tunnel across the world, encountering the colossal elephants that support the quarters of the earth. Finally they discover the horse peacefully grazing near the meditating Kapila. Mistaking the sage for the thief, they rush him with weapons and accusations. Kapila merely utters a powerful sound, and the princes are instantly reduced to ashes—an example of divine power confronting arrogant force.

highlight_spans.why: Celestial beings appeal to Brahma as the princes’ destructive search disrupts the cosmic order.
Brahma reveals the crucial truth: the sage Kapila is a manifestation of Vasudeva and the princes are destined to perish by his wrath.
The princes encounter the colossal elephants that uphold the quarters of the earth—an important mythic cosmology moment.
The princes angrily accuse Kapila of stealing the horse, charging him with weapons and insults.
The climax: Kapila utters a single sound and the immense army of Sagara’s sons is instantly reduced to ashes.

top_scenes.scene_text: Thousands of Sagara’s princes dig through the earth like a living storm while gods and celestial beings watch in alarm from the heavens.
The princes discover a colossal world-supporting elephant towering like a mountain beneath the earth, its movement causing the world above to tremble.
The meditating sage Kapila sits radiant beside the grazing sacrificial horse as the furious princes charge him, only for a flash of divine power to reduce them to ashes.
